sections.rawHeading: 1 · Licensing (GOV — high confidence on scope; medium on amounts)
sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.confidenceNote: high confidence on scope; medium on amounts
sections.markdown: Wisconsin credentials **permit-pullers on 1–2 family dwellings, not chimney contractors.** Under **Wis. Stat. § 101.654(1)(a)**, "no person may obtain a building permit" under the one- and two-family dwelling code unless the person annually holds a DSPS certificate of financial responsibility (the **Dwelling Contractor** certification) and completes continuing education; DSPS says the certificate holder must employ a certified **Dwelling Contractor Qualifier (DCQ)**. **§ 101.654(1)(b) exempts an owner who resides (or will reside) in the dwelling and pulls a permit for work on it.** The requirement is tied to the permit, not to new construction only — so if a chimney rebuild or reline on a UDC-covered dwelling requires a building permit, the contractor pulling it needs the Dwelling Contractor certification (our reading of the statute text; confirm with DSPS before stating it as settled). Bond/insurance options (July pass: $25,000 bond or $250,000 liability insurance) and the DCQ course (July pass: 12 hours + test) were **not re-verified**. Work that needs no permit — sweeping, most repairs, and work on pre-June-1980 dwellings outside UDC scope — needs **no state credential at all**; **Wisconsin has no home-improvement or chimney license**, only consumer rules (ATCP 110). Lookup: DSPS credential search.

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: The Dwelling Contractor credential is about financial responsibility and code accountability — **nothing chimney-specific** — and chimney sweeping/non-permit repair needs no credential. Individual certs (CSIA CCS, C-DET; NCSG CCP/CCR) are the only competence signal.

sections.rawHeading: 3 · Home sale (GOV statute — high; form wording — medium, not re-fetched)
sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.confidenceNote: statute — high; form wording — medium, not re-fetched
sections.markdown: **Real Estate Condition Report, Wis. Stat. §§ 709.02–.03**: the owner must furnish a completed statutory report for most residential transfers. The July research reported that the report asks whether the owner is aware of defects in a **woodburning stove or fireplace**, defects caused by a fire in a stove or fireplace, and smoke-detector-law violations — **the item wording sits in a table not rendered in the sources reachable in September and was not re-confirmed.** Actual-knowledge basis. No inspection is mandated at transfer; NFPA 211 Level 2 stays a NATIONAL STANDARD.

sections.rawHeading: 4 · Consumer remedies (GOV — high on damages; medium on cancel details)
sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.confidenceNote: high on damages; medium on cancel details
sections.markdown: **Home Improvement Practices, ATCP 110** (DATCP) sets home improvement contract requirements (ATCP 110.05) and contract cancellation and return-of-payment rules (ATCP 110.07); the July research reported a **3-business-day right to cancel** for solicited contracts — exact scope not re-verified. ATCP 110 is an order under **Wis. Stat. § 100.20**, and **§ 100.20(5)** gives any person suffering pecuniary loss from a violation **twice the amount of the pecuniary loss, plus costs including a reasonable attorney fee**. Complaints: DATCP + AG.

sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.markdown: Wisconsin runs a **statewide Uniform Dwelling Code (UDC), SPS 320–325** — per DSPS, "the statewide building code for one- and two-family dwellings built since June 1, 1980," enforced in all municipalities. It is Wisconsin's own administrative code (not a straight IRC adoption; exact model-code references in SPS 320 not re-verified). **Key limit for chimney content: homes built before June 1, 1980 sit outside UDC scope** — permit rules for them are local. On UDC-covered homes, chimney relines, rebuilds, and solid-fuel appliance installs are generally permit work; routine sweeps and like-for-like caps generally are not.

sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.markdown: **Wis. Stat. § 101.647** requires the owner of a residential building (dwellings with an attached garage, fireplace, or fuel-burning appliance; tourist rooming houses excluded) to install a functional CO detector **"in the basement of the dwelling and on each floor level except the attic, garage, or storage area"**; buildings permitted after Feb 1, 2011 with utility service need electrically powered detectors with battery backup; owners must respond within 5 days to written notice of a non-functional detector, and occupants must maintain detectors in their units. Broad standing coverage; **no statewide pre-sale certificate** found. A permitted chimney job is the natural moment to verify alarms.

sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.markdown: No statewide burn-ban regime; outdoor wood boilers regulated locally in many towns. **Northern Wisconsin has among the highest wood-heat density in the country** — a core market.

sections.title: Scam patterns and enforcement
sections.markdown: DATCP and the AG pursue home-improvement fraud under ATCP 110 / § 100.20; the door-knock "we noticed your chimney" pitch is a textbook solicited-contract scenario. **Specific WI chimney-sweep enforcement actions: NOT CONFIRMED** — patterns, not names.

sections.title: Season calendar
sections.markdown: Cold statewide, severe in the north. Burn season ~Oct–Apr (longer up north). Rush: SEP–NOV. Best booking: APR–JUN.

sections.title: Price seeding (internal)
sections.markdown: WI labor near or slightly below national; Milwaukee/Madison metros near national. Use national ranges until listings data.

story.heading: The story
story.markdown: Wisconsin credentials the people who **pull permits** on your house, not the ones who **clean and repair the chimney** — the Dwelling Contractor certificate is about financial responsibility and code accountability, and sweeping or non-permit repair sits entirely outside it. The state pairs that gap with real protections: a **uniform statewide dwelling code** (for homes built since mid-1980), **double damages for home-improvement rule violations**, and a **seller condition report that names the fireplace and woodstove.** It lands in the same family as Illinois (comparison) — no chimney license, but a disclosure that actually discloses — in one of the highest wood-heat markets in the country.

faq.q: What should I check before hiring a chimney company in Wisconsin?
faq.a: State licensing: Dwelling Contractor cert required to pull a 1–2 family dwelling building permit (Wis. Stat. 101.654; owner-occupants exempt); NO home-improvement/chimney license. Registration or credential: cert regime + ATCP 110 duties. Seller disclosure at sale: YES — § 709.02–.03 (fireplace/woodstove item per July pass). Right to cancel a sale made at your home: YES per July pass (ATCP 110.07 — details not re-verified). Carbon monoxide alarm law: broad (§ 101.647, basement + every floor). Where to check a contractor: DSPS credential search. Then ask the eight questions below, get the inspection findings in writing with photos, and never sign for "emergency" work on the day of a door-knock.

faq.q: Is a chimney inspection required when a home sells in Wisconsin?
faq.a: Real Estate Condition Report, Wis. Stat. §§ 709.02–.03: the owner must furnish a completed statutory report for most residential transfers. The July research reported that the report asks whether the owner is aware of defects in a woodburning stove or fireplace, defects caused by a fire in a stove or fireplace, and smoke-detector-law violations — the item wording sits in a table not rendered in the sources reachable in September and was not re-confirmed.

faq.q: Can I cancel a chimney contract I signed at my door in Wisconsin?
faq.a: Home Improvement Practices, ATCP 110 (DATCP) sets home improvement contract requirements (ATCP 110.05) and contract cancellation and return-of-payment rules (ATCP 110.07); the July research reported a 3-business-day right to cancel for solicited contracts — exact scope not re-verified. ATCP 110 is an order under Wis. Stat. § 100.20, and § 100.20(5) gives any person suffering pecuniary loss from a violation twice the amount of the pecuniary loss, plus costs including a reasonable attorney fee.
